$comment: Q3/OA material -> roughness and metalness, hand-checked against the images. prefixRules apply in order and the first match wins; `entries` override them by exact material name. Every in-scope material must be covered or `node tools/material-matrix.ts --check` fails. `metalness` is a bit, because for this asset set it is one: a texel is metal or it is not, and the few genuine boundaries are hard paint edges a mask states better than an inference does. `roughness` is the level; the generated ORM supplies variation around it, scaled by `variation` (see tools/pipeline/orm.ts). `normal: "drop"` refuses a generated normal map for surfaces where one is meaningless or double-counts geometry the model already has.
$why: D-092 measured the network's metalness as anti-informative -- it segments by shape rather than material, and returns 0.11 and 0.96 for the same stone wall depending on how it was framed -- and its roughness as contributing nothing to the round trip while being just as unstable. Both are therefore data here rather than inference. This is also the objection shader-to-pbr.ts records against name-based guessing: a table that was hand-checked against the artwork is not a heuristic, and it is the override channel that makes generating the other two channels in bulk safe.

prefixRules.note: Concrete: concrt, concrtcracka, concrtmould, step. Rough grey aggregate.
wood01, woodenbarrier -- planks and a slatted barrier.
The whole dirty-outdoor set: mud, sand, moss, roots, weathered stone tiles and steps. Nothing in it is a conductor and nothing in it is smooth.
Light panels. The visible surface is diffusing glass over a bright interior, and most of these carry an emissive as well.

Rust is iron oxide and a dielectric. Calling a rusted surface metal is the single most common way to get a PBR set wrong -- it looks like a mirror wherever the paint has failed, which is the opposite of what corrosion does.
Pewter, the port's own worked example: F0 goes from 0.04 to the albedo, 5.5x on the direct highlight at every roughness.
Tin, referenced through tcGen environment in Q3. The fake reflection is gone; the metal it was standing in for is real now.
The only near-mirror in the world set.
atech2_c, atech3_a -- painted tech panelling, scuffed. Paint over metal is a dielectric.
Jump-pad plate, hazard-striped steel.
Cloth banners.
Riveted structural beams.
Brown painted-and-worn steel. Dark and low contrast, which is why it is in the pilot set.
Wood panelling.
The rest of e7 is brick and dressed stone: bricks01, brickfloor01, sbrickfloor and variants, walldesign01.

Diamond-plate spawn pad.
drk_brnbrick.

proto_brik, skull2, streetbricks14.

Bracers.
Skin, hair, cloth and painted armour. Where a character has a genuinely metal part it is on its own material and is named above.
Ammunition boxes and canisters, all pressed metal.

Powerup shells and rings -- moulded plastic in the artwork.
Team Arena weapon world models: nailgun, proxmine, vulcan.
Every weapon skin. They are mixed materials -- grips, lenses, painted panels -- but metal is the dominant area on all eleven and metalness is one bit per material.

redArmor.note: Q3 armour is a lacquered metal shell and reads as one. The grey shoulder spheres on the same image are not, but metalness is one bit and the shell is the dominant area.

yellowArmor.note: As redArmor. Gold rather than red, and the case where getting the bit right is most visible: F0 becomes the albedo, so the highlight takes the colour instead of staying white.

textures/acc_dm3/rivets.note: Riveted steel plate. Pilot texture: the network returned metalness 0.01 for it, which is the wrong answer for the most unambiguously metal surface in the world set.

textures/acc_dm3/cop.note: Rusted steel panel under hazard striping. Pilot texture, and the clearest instance of the network segmenting by shape: it returned a clean binary mask of the raised cross, where cross and surround are the same metal.

textures/e8/e8_base1c.note: Brick, despite sharing a prefix with the steel hatch e8_base1. The trailing `c` is a variant letter, not a suffix on the same material, which is the failure mode prefix rules have and the reason entries win.

textures/gothic_block/mkc_evil_e3window.note: Stone surround with a lit grille; the stone is the surface.

textures/gothic_block/pulpywalla.note: Organic wall, not masonry, despite living in gothic_block.

textures/base_light/proto_light.note: Unlike the rest of base_light this is mostly its metal bezel rather than its lens.
